title: Mandarin-Lemon Ponzu-Style Glaze
description: Mandarin and lemon juices give this lightly thickened Japanese-style dipping sauce a fresh, yuzu-like aroma.

ingredients.name: low-sodium mushroom broth
ingredients.note: For a plain infusion, steep sliced mushrooms in hot water, strain and add no salt. Estimate assumes 15 mg sodium per cup.

ingredients.name: Sushi Chef mirin sweetened sake
ingredients.note: Estimate uses the label with 0 mg sodium and 50 calories per tablespoon.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

steps.title: Set aside the fresh citrus
steps.text: Combine {mand}, {le}, {lz} and {rv} in a heatproof cup to preserve their fragrance.

steps.title: Start the glaze
steps.text: Simmer {mu}, {mi} and {a} for 3 minutes. Stir in the citrus mixture and bring just back to a simmer.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Use as a warm dipping glaze for poached fish and asparagus, or spoon it over a mild seafood bowl.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 5 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, replace the lemon juice and vinegar with water and keep the mandarin juice and lemon zest. Nutrition counts the full mirin before simmering. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 32 kcal, 0.2 g protein, 7.3 g total carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 115 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 27 kcal, 0.2 g protein, 6.0 g total carbohydrate, 0.0 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 25 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.
